answer: Archival custody: each identity is assigned a distinct slice of deep history, one relic block each, and must answer random spot-checks about its contents on demand. Two masks cannot share a slice, because whoever fails the same spot-check exposes the pooled copy. Custody must stay retrievable for the whole term, not merely shown once, so the cost per identity is persistent storage of unique material, and N clones need N separate archives rather than one. Slow to build as a glacier, cold as tundra, but it holds.
